title: Extract a specified baseline face law with logarithmic accuracy cost
statement: For a supplied integral support D(x)=n.x-b>=0 on Gamma with n.m=b, the existing exact local mean witness has all its positive-weight atoms on Gamma_F={D=0}. At lambda0=m+1 choose such y; the existing product-Poisson atom bound gives P0(Gamma_F)>=P0(y)>=exp(-K), hence pi0(Gamma_F)>=exp(-K). For t=2^-T, lambdaT_i=(m_i+1)t^n_i is ordinary rational, and piT(x)=pi0(x)t^D(x)/E_pi0 t^D. Its conditional face law is exactly piF=pi0(.|Gamma_F), and off-face probability=TV(piT,piF)<=t exp K. Product-Poisson first moments and the face anchor pay |E_piT X_i-E_piF X_i|<=2t(m_i+1)exp(2K). The stated T gives TV/mean errors<=epsilon with O(T||n||1) explicit extra bits, including negative normals. This approximates the BASELINE FACE-CONDITIONED mean, not arbitrary m. Given multiple supporting equalities, sum their nonnegative integral gaps; the same proof covers their intersection with all normal costs paid.

Conditional arbitrary-tangent lift additionally pays supplied numerical B, P_R(L+B), ordinary exponent output and all asserted slice inequalities; none are free.
